baseline_assumptions: Middle-school learner with basic coding; no learner diagnosis observed.
Week 1 is a foundation, not full contest mastery.

goals.description: Reason about shape, axis and array manipulation as a contest foundation.
Use a short function contract, missingness and returned values.
Use the agreed weekly written assessment format.

comparisons.assessment_method: Review of assigned task text, not observed student work.
comparisons.answer_conditions: Existing lesson requests examples to be hidden for the new-input check; teacher notes hold keys.
comparisons.allowed_support: Student records hints or help; actual assistance is unobserved.
comparisons.competency: Distinguish axis exchange from a reshape with the same resulting shape.
comparisons.difference: The lesson shows reshape and transpose and assigns changed shapes, but no identified question compares equal-shaped outputs to decide whether axes were exchanged.
comparisons.rationale: A small counterexample would require choosing and justifying the operation; this is a foundational bridge, not a claim to cover PyTorch.

theory.claim: Shape alone does not fix how input positions map to output positions.

problem_refs.locator: Written question 2 input/output and label-tie rule

comparisons.difference: The original asks the learner to modify a supplied mean function with detailed hints; no identified short standalone function-specification task combines missing-value treatment, return and edge case without a supplied solution.
comparisons.rationale: A beginner-scale specification and independent checks can bridge to later full algorithmic tasks without requiring K-NN in week 1.

theory.claim: A function contract includes the meaning of input, return and specified boundary behavior.
